sentences: In Babergh and Mid Suffolk, in eastern England, historic roofs do not all look alike.
Some rise steeply. Others sit noticeably lower.
Older timber-framed buildings here were probably roofed with thatch or oak shingles, depending on which materials were available.
Longstraw thatch, the most traditional covering in these districts, is laid at a steep pitch of about fifty degrees.
Eventually, clay peg tiles replaced some of these thatched roofs.
Plain clay tile roofs are fairly steep too, typically forty-five degrees or more.
Materials also began to travel further.
From the eighteenth century, clay pantiles were used more commonly, as moving materials around the country became easier.
In the nineteenth century, the railways meant that slate from Wales, Cornwall and Cumbria was often used here.
Slate roofs here are usually pitched at around thirty degrees, and slate is more effective than smaller tiles at a lower pitch.
Thatch, clay tile and slate each have a typical pitch.
These are tendencies, not rules, and not every building followed the same path.
But the pitch of an old roof can still be a clue to its covering.
